metadata.title: Nvidia stock continues to fall after massive rally, Jensen Huang apologizes to employees

content.text:
Nvidia's (NVDA) stock fell 8% at the open on Wednesday, continuing to reverse from a strong 31% rally on Monday, after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. On Tuesday, the stock fell 7%.
In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board.
In an interview on Monday, President Trump said he had spoken "directly and indirectly" with the board and "convinced" them to make a deal. Top administration officials also reportedly assured the Nvidia board that Huang wasn't a national security risk and wasn't facing alleged chip-smuggling charges.
"I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement.
- Grace O'Donnell
Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia employees in companywide meeting: NYT
The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees during an hourlong, companywide meeting, stating that his actions were "not acceptable" and violated Nvidia's code of conduct. Huang also said that he was in therapy.
"I made some terrible mistakes," Huang said, per the Times. "I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids, and of course, I hurt all of you."
Huang, however, pushed back against the notion that he was a "tech bro" and above the code of conduct.
He also said his return wasn't the result of the board caving to pressure from President Trump. "That is completely untrue," Huang reportedly said, claiming instead that the board "gathered facts" — including that the DOJ didn't consider him a national security threat — and evaluated whether he deserved a second chance.
- Grace O'Donnell
Rep. Meeks calls for Jensen Huang to testify at House public hearing
Rep. Gregory Meeks, a ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and New York Democrat, called on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify at a public hearing for the House, adding another request for Huang to answer questions on Capitol Hill.
Huang is already scheduled for a transcribed interview with Meeks and the committee chairman, Rep. Brian Mast, next week. Huang is also confirmed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next week.
"Americans deserve answers to the profound questions that are continuing to emerge about NVIDIA and our national security," Meeks wrote. "President Trump's intervention to reinstate Jensen Huang as NVIDIA's CEO raises even more concerning questions about the administration's own role, questions the American people deserve to hear answered in public."
- Ben Werschkul
Huang faces 3 camps of GOP skeptics ahead of congressional grilling
President Trump's full-throated support for Jensen Huang and his reinstatement atop Nvidia (NVDA) has not been matched by Republican lawmakers, who say they intend to keep the pressure on the chipmaker.
The objections broadly fall into three categories. A handful of Republicans say it was a mistake to reinstate Huang as CEO. Another group says they have serious concerns and feel that US national security has been compromised. And a third group says simply that they have unanswered questions about the whole affair.
According to a Yahoo Finance tally, a majority of the 13 Republican senators whom Huang will face next week on the Senate Banking Committee have offered at least a promise of tough questions, and two members have even said Huang should not be in the CEO chair.
North Dakota Republican Kevin Cramer recently posted that the legal cloud was "risk enough to not rehire Huang," while Nebraska's Pete Ricketts said his "behavior does not support reinstatement." Both will have time to question Huang.
The hearing will be overseen by Chair Tim Scott of South Carolina, who said in his own statement that national security will be "central to the committee's oversight."
- Grace O'Donnell
Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say
Reuters reports:
Nvidia's board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday.
The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment, these people said.
Nvidia said on Monday that after talks with senior US officials, its board "is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
… The situation undercuts the board's standing, said New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who helps manage retirement funds that hold some 5 million Nvidia shares.
"They told us flatly that he would not be coming back. They have done a total 180 without any explanation, or any indication that concerns about legal and other liabilities have been resolved," Levine said in a telephone interview.
"They have proven they're not independent, and that is the defining quality that we need from any board," he said.
- Grace O'Donnell
Nvidia stock down over 7% in afternoon trading
Nvidia stock is bouncing off its session lows, but shares remain down over 7% as the chipmaking giant gives back some of its gains made on Monday.
The broader chip sector faced selling pressure as investors rotated out of tech and assessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the market's massive rally the day before.
145.45 -9.93 (-6.39%)As of 10:00:06 AM EST. Market Open. - Grace O'Donnell
DOJ official says Attorney General Todd Blanche spoke with Trump about Nvidia
A Department of Justice official said that President Trump spoke with Attorney General Todd Blanche over the weekend and that the DOJ had no evidence of any wrongdoing by Jensen Huang or Nvidia.
In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump stated that Nvidia asked "for assurance on the national security threat."
"And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know. And we know a lot," Trump said Monday.
- Grace O'Donnell
Jensen Huang's return 'the least bad option' for Nvidia: Analyst
Seaport Research Partners senior analyst Jay Goldberg weighed on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, telling Yahoo Finance that it was "probably the least bad option for Nvidia."
Still, he noted, "a lot of the issues that I talked about a month ago before we had all of this drama, still exist, right? There are still real questions about their growth prospects and their reliance on some questionable sales to Asia and their their questionable financing deals across the industry. So I certainly still have a lot of questions."
Watch the interview below:
- Brian Sozzi
Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia. Should AMD be worried?
When it comes to the AI trade, this has been the year of AMD (AMD). AMD's stock has sizzled, up 112% year to date compared to an 11.5% drop for its top rival Nvidia.
As Nvidia's (NVDA) founder Jensen Huang has been embroiled in scandal and the tech trade has been pressured, AMD shares have hung tough. The stock is down 12.2% over the past month versus a 22% decline for Nvidia.
The biggest question for AMD right now is this: Does Huang's stunning return as CEO of Nvidia mean bad news for AMD in 2027 and beyond?
Pros think AMD will be just fine, for now.
"I don't see how this changes it completely," Moor Insights & Strategy founder Patrick Moorhead said on Sozzi Unleashed. "I was saying early on when Jensen left that nothing changes for 18 months. And the reason is the supply chain is locked, the wafers are locked, data center configurations are locked around Nvidia design. So nothing would change, I think, if Jensen had been removed permanently."
- Brian Sozzi
Nvidia's longtime CFO and now former interim CEO Colette Kress was left in the dark about Jensen Huang's return: Report
Colette Kress has been the CFO of Nvidia (NVDA) since 2013, helping to build the company at the center of the AI boom alongside founder and public face Jensen Huang. She stepped into the line of fire for 12 days as interim CEO while Huang worked behind the scenes to return.
She withstood fresh reports of Huang berating her in meetings, and President Trump saying in an interview that she did a poor job in her post-earnings TV interview last week.
In the end, Nvidia's longtime CFO Colette Kress — a widely respected figure on Wall Street — has been left holding the bag.
And, apparently, left out of the loop on Huang's return.
"The talks that culminated in an Nvidia board meeting late on Sunday were so secretive that even interim chief executive officer Colette Kress was kept out of the discussions," a new report on Tuesday from the Financial Times said, citing people familiar with the matter.
- Jennifer Schonberger
Nvidia rebound revives rate-hike bets, testing Fed Chairman Warsh
When stocks tanked last week, Wall Street briefly bet the Federal Reserve would ease up on interest rate hikes. Now Monday's massive rebound — sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia — has revived bets on at least two more interest rate hikes.
Yet with AI stocks still off their highs, the sector's volatility is emerging as a critical test for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and the central bank's path for rate hikes.
"AI stress is not mostly due to the Fed. But it is not a coincidence it is occurring when the Fed is hiking," said Krishna Guha, head of central banking and the economy for Evercore ISI. "Talk of 50-basis-point hikes or faster tightening adds to stress. Fed Chair Warsh not talking is a problem. It leaves the market guessing: Is he a hardcore hawk or a market-sensitive hawk? The gap is filled by others whose views can lag the leadership."
"This is a serious test for Warsh," Guha added.
- Grace O'Donnell
Jensen Huang's return revives an old Wall Street trade: Bet on the comeback CEO
Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports:
Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia (NVDA) could be good for more than a one-day pop in its stock price. Just look at the evidence from the case studies on the returns of founders like Apple's (AAPL) Steve Jobs, Starbucks' (SBUX) founder Howard Schultz, and Charles Schwab's (SCHW) founder Charles Schwab.
A new analysis of six high-profile CEO returns by Rand Group Research found that four of the six companies outperformed the S&P 500 over the three years after their leaders returned.
The biggest winner was Apple, where Steve Jobs' return in September 1997 was followed by a staggering 414% stock gain, versus 59% for the S&P 500 (^GSPC). The stock price gain reflected Jobs' innovation streak, which led to world-changing products like the iPhone and iPod.
There were exceptions, however.
Disney (DIS) shares rose just 14% after Bob Iger returned in 2022, badly trailing the S&P 500's 67% gain, while Under Armour (UA) has fallen 40% since Kevin Plank returned in 2024.
The takeaway for Nvidia investors? A founder's return can be a powerful catalyst, particularly when that founder has a deep understanding of the business and a track record of creating shareholder value.
But it's no guarantee. Jensen Huang has the opportunity to join a pretty impressive comeback club — but he'll still have to deliver.
- Grace O'Donnell
Nvidia shares slide 5% as premarket trading indicates 'turnaround Tuesday'
Nvidia shares slid 5% on Tuesday, retreating from yesterday's monster 31% rally.
As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre points out, "turnaround Tuesday" is pretty par for the course. He writes:
The old Wall Street saying that Tuesday undoes Monday has a point. In the 20 times since 1993 that the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) opened Monday 2% or more higher, it rose the next day only 9 times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. By Friday, it was a coin flip.
Patience usually paid. A year later, SPY was higher in 17 of the 20 cases, with a typical gain of about 26%.
The bad cases were really bad, though. In a quarter of them, SPY fell 12% or more within three months. Five of the 20 came in the fall of 2008.
145.45 -9.93 (-6.39%)As of 10:00:06 AM EST. Market Open. - Ines Ferré
Elon Musk on his support for Jensen Huang: 'Fair-weather friends are worthless'
Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk once again came out in support of his friend Jensen Huang on Monday after Nvidia's board unanimously decided to reinstate Huang as CEO. Musk also took a swipe at those who may not have stood by Huang as publicly or forcefully as he did.
"Everyone is your friend when the chips are up, but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends," Musk wrote on X on Monday in response to a post about his support for Huang. "Fair-weather friends are worthless," Musk added.
Earlier on Monday, Musk immediately responded to the news that Nvidia's board had reinstated the founder as CEO, writing, "It is done." Later, he added, "The mistake has been corrected."
Musk was one of Huang's biggest supporters throughout the ordeal that led to Huang's resignation. He was also vocal about a campaign to bring back Huang, citing a circulating petition.
- Yahoo Finance
Commerce to add Megaspeed to trade deny list: Semafor
According to Semafor, the Trump administration plans to add Megaspeed to a do-not-trade list designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors.
"The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy."
- Ben Werschkul
'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang
Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said to expect "a stronger hearing than normal" when lawmakers have a chance to grill now-reinstated Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang next week.
"What I want to know is the exact tick-tock of how this all occurred," Gallego said, listing questions such as when Huang learned about suspicions of his paramour's involvement with Chinese intelligence, and whether he purposely helped her company evade a ban on semiconductor exports, as well as President Trump's involvement.
"I think it does bring sharper questions into focus," he added.
Gallego spoke to Yahoo Finance on Monday shortly after the Senate Banking Committee, where Gallego sits as a member, confirmed that Jensen's testimony will go forward on Dec. 3.
- Yahoo Finance
Nvidia's $115B neocloud exposure and what its backstops really cover
In the Loop Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen deep dives into Nvidia's (NVDA) business model for financing neocloud operators and the backstops it guarantees.
- Ines Ferré, Brian Sozzi
Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns
Bernstein analysts were quick to upgrade Nvidia (NVDA) on Monday after the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chipmaker, though Wall Street sees ongoing investigations as a lingering overhang on the company.
The stock surged as much as 32% following Huang's reinstatement. President Trump said he spoke to the board and "convinced" them to reinstate Huang.
Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon and his team, which had downgraded the stock to a Neutral-equivalent Market Perform rating just 11 days ago, rerated the stock as Outperform again as soon as the board announced Huang's return.
"As we remain positive on AI buildout fundamentals, and with Jensen back in the seat, we upgrade today back to [Outperform] (as his exit was the primary reason for the downgrade)," Rasgon wrote.
The analyst maintained a $200 price target, highlighting questions that will likely leave some overhang in place, including ongoing investigations which may limit NVDA's multiple for now.
"While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again-off-again response from the board is, frankly, clown-like," the analysts added, questioning what this says about how the board goes about making other decisions. Read more.
- Yahoo Finance
Nvidia stock: How this strategist would trade Jensen Huang's return as CEO
Slatestone Wealth chief market strategist Kenny Polcari joins Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss Nvidia's stock outlook.
- Yahoo Finance
What does Jensen's return mean for AMD?
Patrick Moorhead joins Yahoo Finance executive editor Brian Sozzi to discuss Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia.
- Daniel Howley
Trump intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO at Nvidia
President Trump personally intervened to help convince the Nvidia (NVDA) board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday.
According to The New York Times, Trump tasked Vice President J.D. Vance with speaking with Huang and the Nvidia board provide assurances that Huang wasn't a national security risk and that he wasn't facing any charges related to alleged chip smuggling to China.
Trump and Huang have developed a close relationship with Huang frequently praising the president's stances on various tech policy issues and Trump lauding Huang's business acumen.
Huang previously resigned from Nvidia following revelations about multiple affairs including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and two reported relationship with Nvidia employees.
During the company's Q3 earning call last week, board chair Harvey Jones said the board did not intent to bring Huang back as CEO.

President Trump personally intervened to help convince the Nvidia (NVDA) board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday.

According to The New York Times, Trump tasked Vice President J.D. Vance with speaking with Huang and the Nvidia board provide assurances that Huang wasn't a national security risk and that he wasn't facing any charges related to alleged chip smuggling to China.
Trump and Huang have developed a close relationship with Huang frequently praising the president's stances on various tech policy issues and Trump lauding Huang's business acumen.
Huang previously resigned from Nvidia following revelations about multiple affairs including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and two reported relationship with Nvidia employees.
During the company's Q3 earning call last week, board chair Harvey Jones said the board did not intent to bring Huang back as CEO.
